papers.title: Target Tailored Forest Damage Inventory (TFDI) - Inventory of damage to young forest in 2022 in Norrbotten, Västerbotten, Jämtland and Västernorrland counties
papers.authors: Sören Wulff, Cornelia Roberge, Mats Walheim
papers.abstract: Inventories of forest damage are carried out within the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) Forests programme. An annual monitoring of the most important sources of forest damage is carried out by the Swedish National Forest inventory (NFI). Although the Swedish NFI is an objective and uniform inventory of forest damage in Swedish forests at national and regional scales, less common or less widespread occurrences of forests pests and pathogens are difficult to survey solely through large-scale monitoring programmes. There is a need for complementary inventories to facilitate timely delivery of relevant information. Thus Target-tailored forest damage inventories (TFDI) aiming at providing data for operational decisions making at local level, and linked to specific damage events were introduced. TFDI’s are developed to give rapid response to requested information of specific damage outbreaks. The TFDIs are carried out in limited and concentrated samples, with flexible but robust methods and design. papers.title: An IoT-enabled environmental informatics framework for real-time crop disease detection using attention-driven deep learning
papers.authors: R. RajiniGanth, P. Ganesh Kumar
papers.abstract: Introduction Crop diseases are a major challenge in agriculture because their early and accurate identification is essential for reducing crop losses and improving productivity. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with deep learning provides an effective approach for automated crop disease monitoring by enabling the collection and analysis of environmental parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. However, accurate fine-grained disease identification remains challenging because of variations in disease symptoms, environmental conditions, and visual characteristics. Methods This study proposes an IoT-enabled deep learning framework for automated crop disease detection and classification. The collected crop images are pre-processed using scaling, normalization, and data augmentation techniques to improve image quality and model generalization. For efficient disease detection, a lightweight attention-driven convolutional neural network-based object detection approach, termed YOLO10-YSTs (You Only Look Once 10-Yield Surveillance Technology), is employed. papers.title: Ensemble species distribution modeling and InVEST-based habitat quality assessment for Cupressus funebris under climate change: identifying refugia, ecological security patterns, and conservation priorities in China
papers.authors: Kouame Kouassi Lemouel, Zhihang Zhuo, 邓欣祺, Rulin Wang, Boyang Zhang
papers.abstract: Abstract Cupressus funebris , an indigenous and ecologically important conifer in China, is increasingly endangered by climate change and habitat fragmentation. Using an ensemble species distribution model (BIOMOD2), we projected current and future habitat suitability under three climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5) for the 2050s, 2070s, and 2090s. We integrated 355 occurrence records and bioclimatic variables using 12 algorithms. We also used the InVEST Habitat Quality model to assess current habitat quality and degradation, and constructed an ecological security pattern from habitat patches and resistance surfaces. This framework identified climate refugia and priority conservation zones. Random Forest performed best (AUC = 0.92 ± 0.02, TSS = 0.85 ± 0.03). Temperature seasonality (Bio04) and minimum temperature of the coldest month (Bio06) were the main climatic drivers. Results show severe range contractions under all scenarios: habitat loss ranges from − 28.5% (SSP1-2.6) to − 62.4% (SSP5-8.5) by the 2090s, with elevational shifts of 180–310 m. papers.title: Predicting the potential habitat suitability of Phloeosinus aubei Perris in China using BIOMOD2
papers.authors: S. Ahmad, Xinqi Deng, Habib Ali, Quanfu Jiang, Zhihang Zhuo
papers.abstract: Abstract Phloeosinus aubei Perris, a bark beetle of increasing concern in China, poses significant threats to Cupressaceae species in both natural and managed landscapes. This study used 69 spatially thinned occurrence records and 10 environmental predictors with BIOMOD2 to predict its potential habitat suitability under current and future climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5). The ensemble model showed robust predictive performance (The Area Under Curve was 0.917, and the True Skill Statistic was 0.813). Variable importance analysis identified the minimum temperature of the coldest month (Bio6), mean diurnal range (Bio2), and human footprint as key drivers. Under current conditions, approximately 36.1% of China’s land area was suitable for P. aubei , with high suitability concentrated in the Yangtze River Basin, Sichuan Basin, and central-eastern provinces. Future projections indicate a 9–23% expansion of suitable habitat by the 2090s and a 350–500 km northeastward shift in the centroid of highly suitable habitat under high-emission scenarios. papers.title: Evolution of machine learning-based species distribution models: Technological development, research trends, and future challenges
papers.authors: Jinchen Xu, Gu Jiqi, Shufei Duan, Yanping Wang, Jie Xie
papers.abstract: Species distribution model (SDM) have become important tools for biodiversity assessment, ecological prediction, and conservation planning. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) have expanded their capacity to analyse complex ecological data. However, the overall development trajectory, knowledge structure, and methodological implications of machine learning-based SDM (ML-SDM) remain insufficiently synthesized. This study provides a systematic overview of ML-SDM research from 2006 to 2025 by integrating bibliometric analysis with methodological synthesis. Using 5224 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, we combined bibliometric statistics, collaboration analysis, co-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, temporal keyword evolution, and qualitative synthesis to investigate research trends, methodological development, knowledge accumulation, and future challenges. The results reveal rapid growth in ML-SDM research and extensive international collaboration, with the United States and China leading in publication output. papers.title: Evaluation of Gallery Injection for Management of Invasive Shothole Borers ( Euwallacea spp.) Associated with Fusarium Dieback in High-Value Trees
papers.authors: Beatriz E. Nobua-Behrmann, John N. Kabashima
papers.abstract: Abstract Invasive shothole borers ( Euwallacea spp.)(ISHB) and their associated fungal pathogens cause substantial damage to urban and riparian trees, creating a need for diverse management approaches to accommodate different infestation scenarios. Gallery injection, a technique in which small volumes of pesticide are delivered directly into active beetle galleries, has not previously been evaluated for ISHB and may provide a localized treatment option that limits pesticide applications to infested portions of the host. The objective of this study was to evaluate gallery injection as a management approach for ISHB, compare the efficacy of different active ingredients delivered using this method, and quantify the volume of solution that could be delivered into active galleries under field conditions. Field trials were conducted on Platanus spp. in Southern California. Active galleries were verified prior to treatment, and beetle activity was assessed following injections. Gallery injections with emamectin benzoate and imidacloprid significantly reduced gallery activity relative to untreated controls, whereas acephate provided intermediate control. papers.title: Detection of zoonotic Cryptosporidium parvum in invasive beavers from southern Tierra del Fuego, Chile
papers.authors: Paola Larrauri Aguilar, Guillermo García Contreras, Gonzalo Cabrera, Cristóbal Arredondo, Catherine Dougnac
papers.abstract: Since their introduction to Tierra del Fuego in 1946, invasive beavers ( Castor canadensis ) have expanded their population and caused extensive environmental degradation across the sub-Antarctic region. Beaver dams have profoundly impacted peatlands, mature sub-Antarctic forests, and watercourses. Here, we report a pathogen in invasive beavers in Patagonia and discuss their potential role as a reservoir of waterborne zoonotic pathogens. We detected Cryptosporidium through microscopy using the Ziehl-Neelsen staining technique in beavers collected from southern Tierra del Fuego. Out of the 105 beavers examined, three tested positive to optical microscopy, which were then identified molecularly as Cryptosporidium parvum by sequence analysis of the 18S ribosomal DNA (rDNA), showing a 2.87% infection rate. Given the potential impacts of Cryptosporidium parvum upon native species, wildlife, and human health, this finding highlights the potential risks associated with the ongoing expansion of beavers into other areas of the sub-Antarctic region. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Wildfire and Fuel Treatments in Utah: A Practical Guide and Outcomes From an Oak-Maple Ecosystem
papers.authors: Annie E. Prescott
papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can be mitigated. One way to reduce wildfire risks and protect life, property, and ecosystem services is through fuel treatments — actions that reduce the amount and arrangement of flammable vegetation through mechanical removal, wildland fire, or other methods. Information on wildfire behavior and fuel treatments is abundant but often scattered, ecosystem-specific and difficult to access. In addition, most research in the Western U.S. has focused on conifer forests, leaving other vegetation types understudied. This research addresses these gaps by summarizing wildfire and fuel treatment information for Utah and examining how fuels treatments and wildfire affect wildlands dominated by Gambel oak and bigtooth maple. Chapter II presents a practical guide to wildfire and fuel management in Utah. It explains how fire is influenced by vegetation, weather, and terrain, and describes the most common methods used to reduce fuels in Utah. Treatments can be a

papers.title: Assessing the range expansion of a generalist carnivore by a novel approach combining questionnaires to experts and dynamic occupancy models
papers.authors: Pablo Ferreras, Esther Descalzo, Miguel Delibes‐Mateos, Francisco Díaz‐Ruiz, María Martínez‐Jauregui
papers.abstract: Abstract Despite the ongoing global biodiversity crisis, the geographic ranges of many mesopredators are expanding, largely driven by their generalist life histories and the decline of apex predators. Quantifying these expansions and identifying their underlying drivers remain challenging and require innovative methodological approaches. We aimed at quantifying the factors driving the recent spatial expansion of the Egyptian mongoose ( Herpestes ichneumon ) at the European edge of its range. We combined occurrence data from three periods (2000–2009, 2010–2015 and 2016–2018) in the central Iberian Peninsula (Spain), collected via questionnaires to environmental rangers, with Bayesian dynamic occupancy models. Responses were obtained from 66% of rangers, covering 91.6% of municipalities (93.9% of the total area), ensuring broad spatial representation. Detection probability increased with the proportion of time rangers devoted to field work. Initial mongoose occupancy showed unimodal relationships with elevation and scrubland cover, peaking at low to intermediate elevations and at intermediate scrubland proportions. papers.title: The infectious disease burden in kidney transplant recipients: a 20-year multicenter cohort study on non-graft-failure hospitalizations in eastern China
papers.authors: Zheng Yang, Guangbiao Xu
papers.abstract: Objective Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) face significantly elevated hospitalization rates, with infections being a leading cause. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the epidemiology, clinical outcomes, trends, and economic burden of non-graft-failure hospitalizations (NGFHs), with a particular focus on infectious diseases, in a large Chinese KTR cohort over two decades. Methods This retrospective multicenter cohort study included all adult KTRs under follow-up at three hospitals in eastern China from 2005 to 2024. Non-graft-failure hospitalizations were defined as admissions for indications other than permanent graft loss requiring return to maintenance dialysis or re-transplantation, and excluding routine surveillance biopsies. The primary outcomes were the causes and rates of hospitalization, length of stay (LOS), in-hospital mortality, and direct medical costs. Hospitalization rates per 100 person-years (PY) were calculated, and multivariable logistic regression with clustered robust standard errors and Firth’s penalized maximum likelihood estimation was performed to identify independent risk factors associated with in-hospital death. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Population growth, numerous factories, and many vehicles are the primary sources of environmental pollution and toxic elements in the industrial city of Arak, Iran. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). Results: The results showed that the mean concentrations of all toxic elements except arsenic had a higher value than the background values in the world. The Top Enrichment Factor (TEF) of toxic elements of nickel, chromium, lead, and copper was higher than other elements. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.authors: Kayleigh Chalkowski, Alexandra Sack, George Wittemyer, Ryan S. Miller, Raoul Keith Boughton
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Understanding where and how far animals move across broad ecological contexts is essential for guiding management decisions in natural resource and animal disease management. Commonly, applications predict movement metrics over spatial extents within existing geolocation datasets, which challenges their utility for landscape-scale management applications. Methods We collated geolocation data from 564 wild pigs spanning 25 studies across 10 states in the United States (U.S.). We summarized the distribution of displacement distances for each wild pig at two scales (net displacement, distance relative to an initial geolocation of residency over three months; daily displacement, distance between day-to-day shifts in where individuals geolocate) in each of four seasons. We fit gamma distributions to the individual-level displacement distributions and derived their mean and dispersion parameters as metrics of displacement magnitude and variation. papers.title: Strengthening coconut ( Cocos nucifera L.) genebanks for a climate-resilient and sustainable future
papers.authors: Shunmugiah Veluchamy Ramesh, Vittal Niral, Kukkehalli Balachandra Hebbar
papers.abstract: Abstract Coconut ( Cocos nucifera L.) is a multipurpose crop that supports millions of livelihoods across tropical regions, yet its genetic resources are increasingly threatened by climate change, emerging pests and diseases and changing production demands. Effective conservation of coconut genetic diversity is therefore essential for ensuring future breeding, climate resilience and sustainable production. This critical review evaluates recent advances in coconut genetic resource conservation, genebank management and emerging technologies supporting germplasm utilization. It examines the current status of global coconut genebanks coordinated through the International Coconut Genetic Resources Network, highlighting the strengths and limitations of existing conservation strategies, including field genebanks, in vitro conservation and cryopreservation. Recent developments in molecular characterization, genomics, artificial intelligence, digital technologies and tissue culture have substantially enhanced germplasm characterization, conservation efficiency and climate-resilient breeding. The centriole as a fourth counter of replicative aging: a systems analysis of ARGUS, an open autonomous platform for lineage-scale surveillance
papers.authors: Ming Yao
papers.abstract: Replicative aging in dividing cells is commonly described through three resettable counters: telomere length, mitochondrial state, and chromatin organisation. We argue for a fourth: the centriole, a conserved microtubule-based organelle that every animal cell either keeps or eliminates. Three lines of evidence motivate the proposal. First, centriole fate is highly stereotyped: in Caenorhabditis elegans about 88% of somatic cells eliminate their centrioles during embryogenesis, and elimination is coupled to cell fate (Kalbfuss & Gönczy, 2023a). Second, centriole age measurably biases division geometry and cell fate in human cells, including asymmetric inheritance in stem cells (Thomas & Meraldi, 2024; Izumi et al., 2026). Third, unlike telomeres, mitochondria, and chromatin, the centriole has no known disposal-and-reassembly pathway in somatic cells, yet nature performs an analogous reset between meiosis I and the first blastomeres, at the cost of haploidization (Pierron et al., 2023). papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.source: OpenAlex / Nova Science Publishers (Nova Science Publishers, Inc.)
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the selective degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. One of the principal pathological hallmarks of ALS is the abnormal cytoplasmic mislocalization and aggregation of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43), a multifunctional RNA-binding protein involved in RNA metabolism and stress granule dynamics. Mutations in the TARDBP gene have been associated with both familial and sporadic ALS and are thought to contribute to altered cellular stress responses, defective RNA processing, and impaired proteostasis. papers.title: Bioactive metal-phenolic network and prebiotic hydrogel synergize with mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for microenvironment-modulating therapy of inflammatory bowel disease
papers.authors: Qi Pan, Pei Li, Yingfeng Gao, Na Zhao, Miao Yu
papers.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MVs) hold great promise for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) therapy. However, oral delivery of MVs therapeutic efficacy is severely compromised by the harsh gastrointestinal environment and the hostile inflammatory milieu, characterized by excessive oxidative stress and dysbiosis. To surmount these biological barriers, we engineered Inu@MPN@MV, a multifunctional oral delivery platform that integrates MVs with a caffeic acid-Fe³⁺ metal-phenolic network (MPN) coating and an inulin-based hydrogel matrix. In this synergistic system, the inulin hydrogel provides gastric protection and enables colon-specific release, while simultaneously functioning as a prebiotic to foster a beneficial microbial niche. Concurrently, the MPN coating endows the vesicles with potent ROS-scavenging capabilities, shielding them from oxidative damage and promoting their accumulation at inflamed sites. papers.title: Dual cropping in rice: Integrating Azolla, dhaincha and legumes for sustainable rice production
papers.authors: G Karthika, Elangovan Subramanian, Arumugam Gurusamy, P Meenakshisundaram, P. Arunachalam
papers.abstract: Rice production systems are under increasing pressure to enhance productivity while conserving natural resources and maintaining long-term soil fertility. Dual cropping has emerged as a promising strategy for improving the sustainability of rice production through the integration of compatible companion crops. Common companion crops include Azolla, dhaincha (Sesbania spp.) and grain legumes. These systems improve the use efficiency of land, water and nutrients while reducing dependence on synthetic fertilisers. This review synthesises current knowledge on rice-based dual cropping systems, focusing on their ecological basis, agronomic performance and environmental benefits. The review analyses the impact of weather conditions, soil fertility, water use and cropping calendar on the efficient introduction of dual cropping systems. The advantages of such systems in enhancing nutrient recycling, soil health, soil microbial activity, weed and pest control and resource use efficiency are also discussed. Furthermore, the economic benefits, advancements in technology, existing limitations and potential research areas in rice + Azolla, rice + dhaincha and rice + legume systems are discussed.

Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). After extracting the metals from fiberglass filters by acid digestion based on the ASTM (the American Society for Testing and Materials method), the concentrations of heavy metals were determined by an Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP-OES) device. The human health risk was evaluated according to the US EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) standard method. The obtained data were analyzed by the Spearman correlation and Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) in SPSS. papers.authors: Norman L. Beatty, Sebastián Pita, Bruno Agustin Sansoni-Ruidíaz, Md Mainul Hasan Sarker, Sergio Mendez-Cardona
papers.abstract: Triatoma sanguisuga is the most widely distributed triatomine vector in North America, occurring in at least 23 U.S. states and capable of transmitting Trypanosoma cruzi to humans. Historical morphological variability led to the description of several subspecies, but their taxonomic validity has remained unresolved. We integrated molecular (cytochrome b, n = 58; ITS-2, n = 23) and morphometric (18 characters, n = 82 specimens) data to reassess species boundaries within T. sanguisuga sensu lato. Four species-delimitation methods (GMYC, ABGD, mPTP, hierBAPS) consistently identified four divergent mitochondrial lineages; post-hoc K2P distances among these groups ranged from 4.78 to 8.20% (mean pairwise distances). Florida specimens formed a distinct, strongly supported clade (Group 1; mean K2P 7.19–8.20% from other groups) corresponding to T. sanguisuga var. ambigua Neiva, 1911. Linear discriminant analysis discriminated Florida and non-Florida morphotypes (100% resubstitution accuracy; 80–100% accuracy on small held-out random-forest test subsets), with synthlipsis width providing the strongest diagnostic character (AUC > 0.96). papers.abstract: Introduction Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of irreversible vision loss. It is a complex optic neuropathy, with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) as one of the major risk factors. Recent studies are exploring new devices and technologies for continuous IOP measurement to better monitor glaucoma progression. Rapid and reliable methods for inducing alterations in IOP in laboratory animals may facilitate the development of these technologies. The purpose of this study was to investigate changes in IOP in conscious rabbits placed in different body positions and to assess whether IOP changed with increased duration in each position. Methods The IOP (mean ± SD mmHg) of twelve New Zealand White (NZW) rabbits, six males and six females, was measured at 1-minute intervals for 5 minutes in prone (19.8 ± 3.7), head-up (18.3 ± 2.7), head-down (22.5 ± 3.6), and supine (23.9 ± 3.8) positions. Results IOP differed significantly among all positions (p < 0.001). When IOP measurements obtained from minutes 1 to 5 were compared, no significant differences were observed within any position (p > 0.38). Methods: Treatments consisted of applying MWCNs (2% [W/W]) in the Pb- and Cd-polluted soil that was simultaneously polluted with diesel oil (0, 5, and 10% [W/W]), and the plants used in this study were inoculated with P. indica. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. Results: Soil application of MWCNs at the rate of 2% (W/W) significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil in the drought and salinity (6 dS/m) stress by 11.3% and 15.6%, respectively. papers.abstract: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. papers.abstract: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) is transmitted by Bemisia tabaci through a circulative and replicative pathway and must overcome vector immune defenses to achieve efficient transmission. Oxylipins are important regulators of insect immunity, in which eicosanoids generally promote antiviral responses whereas C18 epoxyoctadecamonoenoic acids (EpOMEs) act as immune suppressors. Although manipulation of insect immunity by plant viruses has been increasingly recognized, the molecular mechanisms by which TYLCV reshapes vector physiology to establish a permissive infection state remain poorly understood. TYLCV infection and localization in B. tabaci were analyzed using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), immunofluorescence assays (IFA), and quantitative PCR. This research analyzes the water-based CSR initiatives of Suzlon Energy Limited and Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) in western Rajasthan. We examined the expression, subcellular distribution, and regulation of MK5 in cardiac ventricular myofibroblasts and myocytes. The copy numbers for MK5 and ERK4 mRNA were comparable in myocytes and myofibroblasts, whereas that of ERK3 was much higher in myofibroblasts. papers.title: Rapid environmental DNA detection with isothermal amplification methods: a comparison with the real-time quantitative PCR in the natterjack toad (Epidalea calamita).
papers.authors: Chieux Abigael, Alessia Guerrieri, Eva Bellemain, Frédéric Boyer, Thomas Merzi
papers.abstract: Species detection relying on environmental DNA (eDNA) traditionally relies on Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR). This amplification technique takes in general a minimum of one hour and requires in most cases access to specialized laboratories and equipment. Isothermal amplification techniques, originating from clinical research, are emerging as rapid and field-deployable alternative methods. Yet, whether their sensitivity, specificity, and cost/time-efficiency are comparable to the traditional real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) remains to be assessed. In this work, we compare the performance of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with qPCR to detect the natterjack toad (Epidalea calamita) from aquatic filtrations. This objective was achieved in three steps. First, we developed LAMP and RPA primers specific to the target species based on its mitochondrial genome. Second, we amplified DNA extracts from E. calamita and from tissues of closely related species using real-time fluorescence detection with LAMP, RPA, and qPCR commercially available protocols to evaluate and compare the sensitivity and specificity of the three methods. papers.title: Organic Amendments for Simultaneous Soil Carbon Sequestration and Soil-Borne Pathogen Suppression: Mechanisms and Perspectives
papers.authors: Qudrat Ullah, Esha Arshad, Kainat Fatima, Waqas Haider, Muhammad Qasim
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of soil science and plant nutrition
papers.abstract: The depletion of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the escalating prevalence of soil-borne plant pathogens represent critical challenges to terrestrial biogeochemical stability and global food security. With approximately 24% of terrestrial carbon reserves lost and over US$220 billion in annual crop losses attributed to soil-borne diseases, understanding biotic and geochemical controls on soil health is essential. This review evaluates the dual functionality of organic amendments (agricultural residues, animal manures, and urban biosolids) as drivers of simultaneous carbon restoration and pathogen suppression. We analyze the mechanisms governing these benefits, focusing on the biogeochemical coupling of element cycles and microbiome-mediated processes such as the formation of recalcitrant carbon, organo-mineral protection, and microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE). Biochar applications can increase SOC stocks by 26–33% (11.5–14.6 Mg ha⁻¹), while silicon-modified biochar reduces the bacterial wilt index caused by Ralstonia solanacearum by 73.4%. Furthermore, we examine the geochemical mechanisms of pathogen suppression through antibiosis, resource competition, and signaling disruption.

Methods This study characterized bacterial communities in five compartments of Pinus massoniana (needles, stems, roots, rhizosphere soil and bulk soil) across four stages of pine wilt disease (PWD; healthy, early, intermediate and late) using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and functional prediction. Results The results showed that bacterial community dynamics were significantly influenced by compartment and disease stage. Notably, the stem compartment exhibited substantial changes: Chao1 index significantly increased at the intermediate stage, whereas Chao1, Shannon and Shannoneven indices declined at late stage. Also in stem compartment, the late stage was characterized by marked enrichment of the phylum Proteobacteria, accompanied by elevated relative abundances of the genera Pseudomonas and Methylobacterium .
